findings.source_passage: The unharming sharks, they glided by as if with padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with sheathed beaks.
findings.source_locator: penultimate paragraph, after 'floated on a soft and dirgelike main'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'padlocks on their mouths' image is one of the most critically celebrated and rhetorically distinctive phrases in the entire Epilogue — the 'unharming' and 'savage' epithets and the padlock conceit are all erased, leaving only bare factual residue. This is among the most quoted lines in the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'The unharming sharks, they glided by as if with padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with sheathed beaks.' This line must not be compressed.

findings.source_passage: Buoyed up by that coffin, for almost one whole day and night, I floated on a soft and dirgelike main.
findings.why_it_matters: 'One whole day and night' has a biblical, incantatory rhythm lost by the cut; 'floated' is more precisely elegiac than 'drifted,' which implies passivity without the funereal resonance.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'one whole day and night' and 'floated' rather than 'drifted.'

summary: The erasure of 'padlocks on their mouths' — the epilogue's most famous image — is a high-severity signature loss that requires regeneration.
